subaward_description: THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IS RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOLLOWING RHTP PROJECT: (A) OUTDOOR RECREATION PROGRAM - INCREASE RURAL RESIDENTS’ ACCESS TO AND PARTICIPATION IN FREE, SELF-DIRECTED, OUTDOOR RECREATION ACTIVITIES THAT SUPPORT PHYSICAL EXERCISE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, AND CHRONIC DISEASE PREVENTION THROUGH MINOR ALTERATIONS OF AN EXISTING, 50-MILE, MULTI-MODEL STATE PARK TRAIL TRAVERSING THE STATE’S RURAL NORTHEASTERN REGION AND LOCAL PARTNERSHIPS IN NINE RURAL TOWNS THAT INCREASE PUBLIC POINTS OF ACCESS AND PROMOTE TRAIL USE.

DMHAS IS RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOLLOWING: A. EXPAND ACCESS MENTAL HEALTH MODEL TO ADULTS I. ENSURE TIMELY AND EQUITABLE ACCESS TO PSYCHIATRIC CONSULTATION FOR ADULT PRIMARY CARE PROVIDERS (PCPS), PARTICULARLY THOSE SERVING RURAL AREAS. CONSULTATION ACTIVITIES PROVIDED WILL BE MULTIFACETED, INCLUDING BY PHONE, ZOOM, IN PERSON, WORKSHOPS, AND CASE CONSULTATIONS. CONDUCT A VARIETY OF OUTREACH ACTIVITIES TO ACHIEVE HIGH PROGRAM AWARENESS AND ENROLLMENT AMONG RURAL ADULT PCPS AND FAMILY PHYSICIANS. IMPROVE ACCESS TO MENTAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE SERVICES FOR ADULTS, PRIORITIZING RURAL AND UNDERSERVED AREAS. B. ADULT 23-HOUR CRISIS STABILIZATION UNITS (CSUS) I. ESTABLISH UP TO 4 ADULT 23-HOUR CSUS, INCLUDING TWO RESPITE BEDS IN EACH PROGRAM, AS A DIVERSION FROM HOSPITAL EDS. SITES WILL BE ESTABLISHED IN THE STATE’S RURAL AREAS, WITH THE POTENTIAL OF BEING LOCATED NEAR HOSPITALS IN THOSE AREAS. SERVICES PROVIDED INCLUDE SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT PLANNING, NURSING, MEDICATION MANAGEMENT, CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS, CASE MANAGEMENT, AND PEER SUPPORT. STAFFING INCLUDES PRESCRIBERS, NURSES, LICENSED INDEPENDENT PRACTITIONERS (E.G., LCSW, LPC), ASSOCIATE LICENSED STAFF (E.G., LMSW), PARAPROFESSIONALS, AND CERTIFIED PEER SUPPORT STAFF.

THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE IS RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOLLOWING RHTP PROJECT: A) SEED FUNDING FOR NON-TRADITIONAL FARMING INFRASTRUCTURE - IMPROVE RURAL HEALTH ACCESS AND NUTRITION-RELATED CONDITIONS BY INVESTING IN THE STATE’S LOCAL FOOD SYSTEM AS A PREVENTIVE HEALTH STRATEGY. DOAG WILL ADMINISTER COMPETITIVE GRANTS AND TARGETED INVESTMENTS THAT STRENGTHEN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, FOOD SYSTEM INFRASTRUCTURE, AND PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN FARMS, FOOD ACCESS ORGANIZATIONS, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO INCREASE ACCESS TO FRESH, LOCALLY PRODUCED CT GROWN FOOD, STRENGTHEN RURAL FOOD ACCESS SYSTEMS, AND SUPPORT DIRECT HEALTH SERVICES FOR AGRICULTURAL WORKERS.

ADS IS RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOLLOWING RHTP PROJECTS: PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE DIGITAL LITERACY AND TECHNOLOGY SUPPORT TO OLDER ADULTS AND INDIVIDUALS WITH DISABILITIES. SERVICES INCLUDE ASSISTANCE WITH PERSONAL DEVICES (PHONES, TABLETS, LAPTOPS), ACCESSIBILITY FEATURES, INTERNET ACCESS, ONLINE SERVICES, AND TELEHEALTH. THE PROGRAM WILL ALSO DISTRIBUTE DEVICES (TABLETS/HOTSPOTS), PROVIDE TECH SUPPORT TO SENIOR FACILITIES, AND PILOT A VIRTUAL PLATFORM TO OFFER ONLINE EDUCATIONAL, WELLNESS, AND ENGAGEMENT PROGRAMMING TO RESIDENTS IN THEIR RURAL TOWNS. PROMOTING HEALTHY AGING IN RURAL CONNECTICUT THROUGH ENGAGING EXERCISE - ADMINISTER A 10-WEEK EXERCISE PROGRAM FOR AT-RISK PHYSICALLY INACTIVE OLDER ADULTS (MULTIPLE COMORBIDITIES OR RISK OF FALLS/ILLNESS). CLASSES MEET TWICE WEEKLY, EMPHASIZING STRENGTH, BALANCE, AND FLEXIBILITY EXERCISES AND FALL PREVENTION EDUCATION. HEALTH QUESTIONNAIRES ARE REQUIRED BEFORE AND AFTER THE PROGRAM.

SDE IS RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOLLOWING RHTP PROJECTS: A. HIGH ACUITY SCHOOL-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROGRAMMING CONTRACT/SUBCONTRACT WITH CHILD HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENT INSTITUTE (CHDI) TO DEVELOP TAILORED, COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL MENTAL HEALTH FRAMEWORKS THAT INTEGRATE MENTAL HEALTH PROMOTION, CAPACITY BUILDING, AND ORGANIZATIONAL ASSESSMENTS WITHIN A MULTI-TIERED SYSTEM OF SUPPORTS (MTSS). KEY ACTIVITIES INCLUDE STAFF TRAINING IN TRAUMA-INFORMED PRACTICES AND SUICIDE PREVENTION AND INTEGRATING COMMUNITY-BASED SERVICES. CONTRACT/SUBCONTRACT WITH REGIONAL EDUCATIONAL SERVICE CENTERS (RESCS) TO ENHANCE COLLABORATION, PROVIDE COST-EFFECTIVE EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES AND TRAINING TO RURAL DISTRICTS, AND COORDINATE MENTAL HEALTH TELEHEALTH SERVICES. CONTRACT/SUBCONTRACT WITH CENTER FOR CONNECTICUT EDUCATION RESEARCH COLLABORATIVE (CCERC) (A 17-UNIVERSITY JOINT INITIATIVE) TO RESEARCH AND EVALUATE STUDENT MENTAL HEALTH INDICATORS AND ENSURE DATA QUALITY IN COLLABORATION WITH CHDI, PROVIDERS, AND RESCS. CONTRACT AND/OR SUBCONTRACT WITH RURAL COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH SERVICE PROVIDER(S) TO UTILIZE A BLEND OF TRADITIONAL, TELEHEALTH, AND MOBILE CLINIC SERVICES, BACKED BY ENHANCED LOCAL SUPPORT AND SPECIALIZED RESOURCES LIKE 211 AND 988, TO ADDRESS GEOGRAPHIC BARRIERS AND PROVIDER SHORTAGES.

OEC IS RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOLLOWING RHTP PROJECTS: UNIVERSAL NURSE HOME VISITING EXPANSION, FAMILY BRIDGE I.UTILIZING THE ESTABLISHED EVIDENCE-BASED MODEL, THE FAMILY BRIDGE PROGRAM, BASED ON THE FAMILY CONNECTS INTERNATIONAL MODEL, OEC CONTRACTORS AND/OR SUBCONTRACTORS WILL OFFER ALL REGIONAL FAMILIES WITH NEWBORNS ONE (1) TO THREE (3) NURSE HOME VISITS AND UP TO SIX (6) MONTHS OF COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER SUPPORT. THESE PREVENTION-ORIENTED SERVICES ADDRESS PHYSICAL, MENTAL, AND SOCIAL HEALTH FACTORS. OEC CONTRACTOR(S) AND/OR SUBCONTRACTOR(S) WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THREE (3) KEY FUNCTIONS: 1.EVALUATION. CONTRACTOR AND/OR SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DESIGN AND CONDUCT A FULL FAMILY BRIDGE PROGRAM REVIEW, ANALYZING OUTCOMES AND COST SAVINGS; 2.MARKETING. CONTRACTOR AND/OR SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP AND DELIVER PROMOTION STRATEGIES FOR THE FAMILY BRIDGE PROGRAM'S AVAILABILITY AND SUCCESSES IN NORTHEASTERN AND NORTHWESTERN CONNECTICUT; AND 3.SUSTAINABILITY. CONTRACTOR AND/OR SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP PLANS TO SECURE MULTIPLE FUNDING STREAMS FOR THE FAMILY BRIDGE PROGRAM'S LONG-TERM VIABILITY IN NORTHEASTERN AND NORTHWESTERN CONNECTICUT.

DPH IS RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOLLOWING RHTP PROJECTS: A. MOBILE HEALTH PILOTS - TEND TO ACUTE PATIENT NEEDS WITH GOAL OF AVOIDING ED VISITS AND HOSPITALIZATION. MANAGE CHRONIC ILLNESSES. HELP WITH MEDICATION MANAGEMENT. CONNECT PATIENTS WITH SOCIAL AND COMMUNITY SERVICES. ADDRESS BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, MENTAL HEALTH, AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE. IMPROVE HEALTH FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN. B. MOBILE CLINIC PILOT - CONTRACTORS WILL BE SELECTED VIA AN RFP PROCESS TO SUPPORT THE PURCHASE AND ONGOING STOCKING OF EIGHT MOBILE HEALTH VANS, WHICH WILL BE USED TO PROVIDE PREVENTATIVE CARE, WELLNESS CHECKS, DISEASE MANAGEMENT, DENTAL CLEANING, AND/OR APPLICABLE SERVICES IN RURAL AREAS. TWO MOBILE VANS WILL BE SET ASIDE FOR THE PURCHASE AND USE BY FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBAL NATIONS. C. RURAL PROVIDER INCENTIVES - DPH WILL ADMINISTER THE AWARDS PROGRAM TO INCENTIVIZE HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS TO WORK IN RURAL AREAS, INCLUDING $1 MILLION ANNUALLY SET ASIDE FOR FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBES. PROVIDERS WILL RECEIVE AWARDS TO OFFSET PERSONAL EXPENSES (E.G., CHILDCARE, HOUSING, ETC.) IN EXCHANGE FOR COMMITTING TO A MINIMUM OF FIVE YEARS OF WORK IN RURAL AREAS. D. FORMALIZE CERTIFIED NURSE AIDE (CNA) TRAINING AND MEDICATION ADMINISTRATION TRAINING - FORMALIZE AND EXPAND STATE’S CNA TRAINING TO MAKE IT APPLICABLE TO ALL HEALTHCARE SETTINGS. CREATE INCREASED PRACTICUM OPPORTUNITIES IN RURAL FACILITIES OF ALL TYPES TO DRIVE WORKFORCE PARTICIPATION IN THESE LOCATIONS. FORMALIZE MEDICATION ADMINISTRATION TRAINING THROUGH THE STATE’S COMMUNITY COLLEGES. E. RURAL RESIDENCY DEVELOPMENT GRANT - DPH WILL FUND START-UP COSTS FOR ACADEMIC MEDICAL NSTITUTIONS TO DEVELOPMENT NEW RESIDENCY SPOTS FOR PHYSICIANS IN RURAL AND COMMUNITY MEDICINE.

THE OFFICE OF HEALTH STRATEGY IS RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE FOLLOWING RHTP PROJECTS: A) CONSUMER AI-POWERED CARE MANAGEMENT TOOLS - CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTATION RELATED TO CONNECTICUT AI-POWERED VIRTUAL CARE AND REMOTE PATIENT TRANSFORMATION INITIATIVE THAT WILL MODERNIZE RURAL HEALTHCARE DELIVERY BY SUPPORTING HOSPITALS, FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS FQHCS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND SUD AND INDEPENDENT PRACTICES AND MATERNITY PROGRAMS IN ADOPTING ADVANCED REMOTE MONITORING PLATFORMS. AI-POWERED CARE PATHWAYS AND DIGITAL PATIENT ENGAGEMENT TOOLS, ALL INTEGRATED WITH CONNIE (HEALTH INFORMATION EXCHANGE). B) CT RURAL PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS AND CARE COORDINATION PLATFORM - CONTRACTOR WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR IMPLEMENTATION RELATED TO RURAL PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS AND CARE COORDINATION PLATFORM PROGRAM, WHICH LEVERAGES PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS AND DATA-DRIVEN CARE COORDINATION TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR HIGH-NEEDS PATIENTS SERVED BY RURAL FQHCS. SOW INCLUDES ESTABLISHING ROBUST DATA GOVERNANCE AND PRIVACY FRAMEWORKS, INTEGRATING CLINICAL AND SOCIAL DETERMINANTS DATA FROM STATEWIDE SOURCES, DEVELOPING AND PILOTING ANALYTIC TOOLS AND CARE-EXTENDER MODELS. PROJECT ENCOMPASSES TECHNOLOGY INFRASTRUCTURE SETUP, WORKFORCE TRAINING, ONGOING EVALUATION AND MULTIAGENCY COLLABORATION WITH CLEAR DELIVERABLES. IT ALSO INCLUDES PERSONNEL, TECHNOLOGY, FQHC GRANTS AND INDEPENDENT EVALUATION TO ENSURE SUSTAINABLE EQUITABLE ACCESS TO CARE. C) HIE EXPANSION FOR RURAL PROVIDERS, EMS, AND NURSING HOMES - PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE PROJECT MANAGEMENT FOR HIE EXPANSION FOR RHT, INCLUDING DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING A PROJECT PLAN, BUDGET, TIMELINE, AND COMMUNICATION STRATEGY. THE POSITION WILL OVERSEE ENGAGEMENT WITH RURAL HEALTHCARE ORGANIZATIONS, GUIDING THEIR ONBOARDING, EXECUTING NECESSARY AGREEMENTS, FACILITATING ACCESS TO CONNIE'S DATA SERVICES, AND PROVIDING TRAINING AND SUPPORT TO ENSURE EFFECTIVE TOOL ADOPTION AND UTILIZATION. THE ROLE REQUIRES SERVING AS A PRIMARY LIAISON TO TRACK PROJECT GOALS, COLLABORATING WITH PARTNERS TO IMPROVE RURAL HEALTH OUTCOMES, AND MONITORING AND LEADING EFFORTS TO RESOLVE DATA QUALITY AND TRANSMISSION ISSUES ACROSS PARTICIPATING ORGANIZATIONS, CONNIE'S TECHNOLOGY VENDOR (CSS), EHR VENDORS, AND INTERNAL ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT STAFF. D) RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION THROUGH SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE AND TELEHEALTH INNOVATION - IMPLEMENT A SECURE, CLOUD-BASED IT INFRASTRUCTURE ACROSS RURAL HOSPITALS AND FQHCS IN CONNECTICUT, ENABLING MODERNIZATION OF CLINICAL SYSTEMS, ENHANCED CYBERSECURITY, AND SEAMLESS DATA INTEGRATION. THE PROJECT WILL EXPAND TELEHEALTH SERVICES STATEWIDE, INTEGRATING REMOTE PATIENT MONITORING, VIRTUAL CONSULTATIONS, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH COORDINATION, WITH SPECIAL ATTENTION TO BROADBAND CHALLENGES IN RURAL AREAS. E) CT HEALTHCARE BED CAPACITY TRACKING SYSTEM: (I) ADMINISTER SUB-GRANTS TO SUBRECIPIENTS TO SUPPORT MODERNIZATION OF RURAL HEALTHCARE THROUGH AI ENABLED REMOTE MONITORING AND VIRTUAL CARE SOLUTIONS. (II) ENGAGE CONTRACTOR(S) AND/OR SUBRECIPIENT(S) WHO WILL DESIGN, DEVELOP, AND IMPLEMENT A STATEWIDE, REAL-TIME PLATFORM FOR MONITORING HOSPITAL CAPACITY THROUGH SHARED DATA. (III) ENGAGE CONTRACTOR(S) TO SUPPORT ACTIVITIES THAT LEVERAGE EXISTING DATA SYSTEMS TO IDENTIFY PATIENTS AND COMMUNITIES AT HIGH RISK FOR EMERGENCY VISITS AND AVOIDABLE HOSPITALIZATIONS. (IV) ENGAGE CONTRACTOR(S) TO SUPPORT EXPANSION OF PARTICIPATION IN CONNECTICUT'S HEALTH INFORMATION EXCHANGE, ""HIE,"" CONNIE, BY ASSISTING RURAL AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS WITH ONBOARDING AND TECHNICAL INTEGRATION. (V) ENGAGE CONTRACTOR(S) TO SUPPORT INITIATIVES TO EXPAND TELEHEALTH SERVICES WHICH MAY INCLUDE BUILDING A SHARED IT INFRASTRUCTURE THAT ENABLES RURAL PROVIDERS TO DELIVER CONNECTED, HIGH-QUALITY CARE, REDUCE PREVENTABLE HOSPITAL USE, AND STRENGTHEN THE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF RURAL HEALTH SYSTEMS.

MARSHALL COUNTY EMS IS REQUESTING GRANT FUNDING TO PURCHASE A NEW AMBULANCE TO ENSURE OUR COMMUNITY CONTINUES TO RECEIVE SAFE, RELIABLE, AND TIMELY EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES. OUR CURRENT AMBULANCE FLEET IS AGING, RESULTING IN INCREASED MAINTENANCE COSTS, MORE FREQUENT MECHANICAL REPAIRS, AND A GREATER RISK OF UNEXPECTED EQUIPMENT FAILURES. THESE ISSUES CAN REDUCE AMBULANCE AVAILABILITY, DELAY EMERGENCY RESPONSE TIMES, AND INCREASE OPERATIONAL COSTS THAT WOULD OTHERWISE BE DIRECTED TOWARD PATIENT CARE. A NEW AMBULANCE WILL ENHANCE THE SAFETY OF BOTH PATIENTS AND EMS PERSONNEL BY PROVIDING MODERN SAFETY FEATURES, IMPROVED PATIENT CARE CAPABILITIES, AND GREATER RELIABILITY. UPDATED VEHICLES ARE DESIGNED TO ACCOMMODATE TODAY'S ADVANCED LIFE SUPPORT EQUIPMENT, IMPROVE INFECTION CONTROL, REDUCE PROVIDER FATIGUE THROUGH IMPROVED ERGONOMICS, AND OFFER ENHANCED CRASH PROTECTION. RELIABLE TRANSPORTATION IS ESSENTIAL WHEN RESPONDING TO LIFE-THREATENING EMERGENCIES, TRANSPORTING CRITICALLY ILL OR INJURED PATIENTS, AND PROVIDING INTERFACILITY TRANSFERS. AS A NONPROFIT EMS DISTRICT, MARSHALL COUNTY EMS IS COMMITTED TO PROVIDING HIGH-QUALITY EMERGENCY MEDICAL CARE REGARDLESS OF A PATIENT'S ABILITY TO PAY. RISING COSTS FOR VEHICLE MEDICAL EQUIPMENT AND MAINTENANCE HAVE MADE REPLACING AGING AMBULANCES INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT WHILE MAINTAINING AFFORDABLE SERVICE FOR OUR COMMUNITY.

OHIO'S RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT INITIATIVES TO IMPROVE HEALTH FOR RURAL OHIOANS THROUGH INNOVATION, HEALTHCARE ACCESS, AND PREVENTION. - THE OHIO RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM (RHTP) PRESENTS THIS PLAN TO STRENGTHEN HEALTHCARE ACCESS, OUTCOMES, AND WORKFORCE CAPACITY ACROSS OHIO’S 73 NON-URBAN COUNTIES. THE 4.4 MILLION RESIDENTS LIVING IN THESE RURAL COMMUNITIES ARE IMPACTED BY LIMITED ACCESS TO CARE, HOSPITAL CLOSURES, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, AND HIGH RATES OF CHRONIC AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. RURAL AND APPALACHIAN OHIOANS EXPERIENCE HIGHER RATES OF HEART DISEASE, DIABETES, COPD, CANCER, AND SUICIDE THAN STATE AVERAGES. THIRTEEN COUNTIES ARE MATERNITY CARE DESERTS, AND NEARLY ONE IN FIVE RURAL HOSPITALS IS AT RISK OF CLOSURE. PROVIDER SHORTAGES ARE WIDESPREAD: PRIMARY CARE AVAILABILITY IS NEARLY HALF THAT OF URBAN REGIONS, AND BEHAVIORAL AND ORAL HEALTH GAPS PERSIST. THESE CHALLENGES ARE COMPOUNDED BY LOWER EDUCATION LEVELS, HIGHER POVERTY, AND AN AGING POPULATION—ONE IN THREE RURAL OHIOANS IS OVER AGE 60. OHIO’S PLAN ALIGNS WITH FEDERAL PRIORITIES TO MAKE RURAL AMERICA HEALTHY AGAIN THROUGH SUSTAINABLE ACCESS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, INNOVATIVE CARE, AND TECH ADVANCEMENT. KEY INITIATIVES: RURAL HEALTH INNOVATION HUBS – ESTABLISH CLINICALLY INTEGRATED NETWORKS (CINS) AND REGIONAL CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE LINKING HOSPITALS, CLINICS, EMS, PHARMACISTS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO COORDINATE CARE, REDUCE COSTS, AND EXPAND CAPACITY. LEGISLATIVE REFORMS WILL ALLOW LOW-RISK BIRTHING CENTERS IN RURAL HOSPITALS. EMERGENCY CARE TRANSFORMATION – SCALE A SUCCESSFUL PILOT ENABLING EMS TO PROVIDE TREAT-IN-PLACE OR ALTERNATE-DESTINATION CARE, REDUCING UNNECESSARY EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT USE THROUGH TRAINING, SYSTEM UPGRADES, AND IMPROVED CONNECTIVITY. SCHOOL-BASED HEALTH CENTERS – ESTABLISH CLINICS ON K–12 AND COLLEGE CAMPUSES OFFERING PRIMARY, BEHAVIORAL, DENTAL, AND TELEHEALTH SERVICES FOR STUDENTS AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS, SERVING ALSO AS RURAL CLINICAL TRAINING SITES. OH SEE – EXPAND STATEWIDE MOBILE VISION, HEARING, AND DENTAL CARE BASED ON A 13-COUNTY PILOT TO ENSURE EARLY DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN. RURAL WORKFORCE PIPELINE – BUILD A CONTINUUM FROM HIGH SCHOOL THROUGH PROFESSIONAL TRAINING AND EMPLOYMENT, FEATURING UPSKILLING FOR COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS AND PHARMACISTS, FIVE-YEAR RURAL SERVICE COMMITMENTS, AND PARTNERSHIPS AMONG SCHOOLS, UNIVERSITIES, AND EMPLOYERS. CROSS-CUTTING STRATEGIES: RHTP EMBEDS TELEHEALTH, REMOTE MONITORING, AND INTEROPERABLE ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS ACROSS INITIATIVES. POLICY ACTIONS INCLUDE EXPANDING PHARMACIST SCOPE OF PRACTICE, ESTABLISHING RURAL BIRTHING CENTERS, REINSTATING THE PRESIDENTIAL FITNESS TEST, AND REQUIRING PHYSICIAN NUTRITION CME. MORE THAN 300 PARTNERS (HOSPITALS, FQHCS, UNIVERSITIES, EMS, ASSOCIATIONS) COLLABORATED ON THE PLAN. IMPLEMENTATION WILL OCCUR THROUGH LOCAL PARTNERS WITH STATE OVERSIGHT. SUSTAINABILITY: EACH PROJECT IS DESIGNED FOR LONG-TERM VIABILITY THROUGH BILLABLE SERVICE MODELS, SHARED-SERVICE EFFICIENCIES, AND ALIGNMENT WITH MEDICAID AND VALUE-BASED PAYMENT SYSTEMS. WORKFORCE INCENTIVES, TECHNOLOGY ADOPTION, AND LEGISLATIVE REFORMS WILL ENSURE CONTINUITY BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD. EXPECTED OUTCOMES BY 2031: • ESTABLISH REGIONAL INTEGRATED NETWORKS ACROSS ALL RURAL COUNTIES. EXPANDED RURAL SBHCS. • REDUCE AVOIDABLE EMERGENCY VISITS THROUGH EMS INNOVATION. • IMPROVE DIABETES AND HYPERTENSION OUTCOMES STATEWIDE. • INCREASE THE RURAL HEALTH WORKFORCE BY AT LEAST 20%. • STRENGTHEN MATERNAL, BEHAVIORAL, AND PREVENTIVE CARE ACCESS. CONCLUSION: THIS REPRESENTS A BOLD, DATA-DRIVEN TRANSFORMATION OF RURAL HEALTHCARE IN OHIO. THROUGH TECHNOLOGY, POLICY INNOVATION, AND CROSS-SECTOR COLLABORATION, THE PROGRAM WILL CREATE A SUSTAINABLE MODEL THAT IMPROVES CARE QUALITY, STRENGTHENS THE WORKFORCE, AND ENHANCES HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR RURAL OHIOANS.

OHIO'S RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT INITIATIVES TO IMPROVE HEALTH FOR RURAL OHIOANS THROUGH INNOVATION, HEALTHCARE ACCESS, AND PREVENTION. - THE OHIO RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM (RHTP) PRESENTS THIS PLAN TO STRENGTHEN HEALTHCARE ACCESS, OUTCOMES, AND WORKFORCE CAPACITY ACROSS OHIO’S 73 NON-URBAN COUNTIES. THE 4.4 MILLION RESIDENTS LIVING IN THESE RURAL COMMUNITIES ARE IMPACTED BY LIMITED ACCESS TO CARE, HOSPITAL CLOSURES, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, AND HIGH RATES OF CHRONIC AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. RURAL AND APPALACHIAN OHIOANS EXPERIENCE HIGHER RATES OF HEART DISEASE, DIABETES, COPD, CANCER, AND SUICIDE THAN STATE AVERAGES. THIRTEEN COUNTIES ARE MATERNITY CARE DESERTS, AND NEARLY ONE IN FIVE RURAL HOSPITALS IS AT RISK OF CLOSURE. THE SUB-INITIATIVE WILL UTILIZE A COORDINATED IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY THAT COMBINES ENHANCEMENTS TO VDH-OPERATED MATERNAL HEALTH SERVICES WITH COMPETITIVELY AWARDED COMMUNITY-BASED PROJECTS DESIGNED TO EXPAND ACCESS TO INNOVATIVE MODELS OF PRENATAL, PERINATAL, AND POSTPARTUM CARE. ACTIVITIES WILL FOCUS ON REDUCING BARRIERS TO CARE, STRENGTHENING REGIONAL MATERNAL HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE, IMPROVING CARE COORDINATION, AND INCREASING ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-INFORMED SERVICES THAT IMPROVE MATERNAL AND INFANT HEALTH OUTCOMES. VDH WILL ESTABLISH PROGRAM LEADERSHIP, GRANTS MANAGEMENT, FINANCIAL OVERSIGHT, PERFORMANCE EVALUATION, AND STATEWIDE COORDINATION TO SUPPORT IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SUB-INITIATIVE. WITHIN SELECTED RURAL HEALTH DISTRICTS, FUNDING WILL ENHANCE CLINICAL CAPACITY THROUGH PERSONNEL, EQUIPMENT, AND TECHNOLOGY THAT EXPANDS ACCESS TO PRENATAL SERVICES, PATIENT NAVIGATION, LANGUAGE ACCESS, TELEHEALTH, CARE COORDINATION, AND OTHER SERVICES THAT IMPROVE MATERNAL HEALTH OUTCOMES. ADDITIONAL STATEWIDE INVESTMENTS WILL STRENGTHEN MATERNAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND POSTPARTUM SUPPORT SERVICES WHILE IMPROVING REFERRAL NETWORKS AND ACCESS TO SPECIALIZED MATERNAL CARE. THE MAJORITY OF GRANT FUNDING WILL BE DISTRIBUTED THROUGH A COMPETITIVE REQUEST FOR APPLICATIONS (RFA) PROCESS TO SUPPORT INNOVATIVE COMMUNITY-BASED MATERNAL HEALTH PROJECTS THROUGHOUT RURAL VIRGINIA. ELIGIBLE ORGANIZATIONS WILL IMPLEMENT LOCALLY DRIVEN SOLUTIONS THAT ADDRESS MATERNAL HEALTH CARE GAPS THROUGH COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS AMONG HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, HOSPITALS, RURAL HEALTH CLINICS, FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AND OTHER REGIONAL PARTNERS. PROJECTS MAY INCLUDE MATERNAL HEALTH HUBS, INNOVATIVE PRENATAL AND POSTPARTUM SERVICE DELIVERY MODELS, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES, TRANSPORTATION AND CARE COORDINATION SERVICES, DOULA SUPPORT, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND SUBSTANCE USE SERVICES, TELEHEALTH, MOBILE CARE MODELS, AND OTHER EVIDENCE-INFORMED APPROACHES THAT IMPROVE TIMELY ACCESS TO MATERNAL HEALTHCARE. ALL FUNDED ACTIVITIES WILL INCORPORATE PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENT, CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT, AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING TO SUPPORT LONG-TERM IMPROVEMENTS IN MATERNAL HEALTHCARE DELIVERY ACROSS RURAL VIRGINIA.

subaward_description: THE VDH OFFICE OF EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES (OEMS) WILL ADMINISTER THE COMMUNITY PARAMEDICINE SUB-INITIATIVE UNDER THE COMMONWEALTH’S CMS-APPROVED RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM PROJECT NARRATIVE. PILOT PROJECTS WILL ADDRESS LOCALLY IDENTIFIED HEALTHCARE NEEDS THROUGH EVIDENCE-INFORMED INTERVENTIONS THAT LEVERAGE EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES (EMS) PROVIDERS AS INTEGRATED MEMBERS OF THE HEALTHCARE DELIVERY SYSTEM. REGIONAL EMS COUNCILS WILL SERVE AS REGIONAL IMPLEMENTATION PARTNERS BY SUPPORTING LOCAL COMMUNITIES THROUGHOUT PROJECT PLANNING, DEVELOPMENT, IMPLEMENTATION, AND EVALUATION. WORKING IN COLLABORATION WITH OEMS, REGIONAL EMS COUNCILS WILL FACILITATE STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT, ASSIST WITH PROJECT DEVELOPMENT, PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO AWARDEES, ENCOURAGE REGIONAL COLLABORATION, IDENTIFY IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGES AND BEST PRACTICES, AND SUPPORT PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT ACTIVITIES. THIS REGIONAL SUPPORT STRUCTURE IS INTENDED TO STRENGTHEN LOCAL IMPLEMENTATION WHILE PROMOTING CONSISTENCY, COLLABORATION, AND DISSEMINATION OF SUCCESSFUL PRACTICES ACROSS RURAL VIRGINIA. OEMS WILL PROVIDE OVERALL PROGRAM LEADERSHIP BY ADMINISTERING THE COMPETITIVE FUNDING PROCESS, EXECUTING AND MONITORING PROJECT AGREEMENTS, COLLECTING AND ANALYZING PROGRAM DATA, EVALUATING PROJECT OUTCOMES, COORDINATING STATEWIDE LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES, AND IDENTIFYING SUCCESSFUL MODELS FOR FUTURE EXPANSION AND LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUPPORT IS TO ASSIST ORGANIZATIONS APPLYING FOR FUNDING UNDER THE RURAL HEALTH TRANSFORMATION PROGRAM (RHTP) BY PROVIDING TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO DEVELOP AND SUBMIT APPLICATIONS THAT ALIGN WITH ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA, CLEARLY AND EFFECTIVELY ARTICULATE THEIR VISION, AND DEMONSTRATE FEASIBLE APPROACHES TO IMPLEMENTATION. THIS SUPPORT ALSO AIMS TO STRENGTHEN THE OVERALL QUALITY AND COMPLETENESS OF APPLICATIONS, ADDRESS QUESTIONS OR GAPS THAT ARISE DURING THE APPLICATION PROCESS, AND SUPPORT CURRENT GRANTEES IN MEETING REPORTING REQUIREMENTS AND DOCUMENTING PROGRESS, OUTCOMES AND LESSONS LEARNED. KHI ALSO WOULD WORK WITH KDHE TO IDENTIFY OPPORTUNITIES TO IMPROVE AND STREAMLINE RFPS AND THE APPLICATION PROCESS BASED ON APPLICANT QUESTIONS, RECURRING CHALLENGES AND LESSONS LEARNED THROUGH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. A CORE COMPONENT OF THIS WORK IS TO ASSIST GRANTEES ONBOARDING WITH BDO AND SERVING AS A HELP DESK, PARTICULARLY FOR FIRST-TIME GRANTEES. THE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE HUB IS DESIGNED NOT ONLY TO RESPOND TO INDIVIDUAL QUESTIONS, BUT ALSO TO STRENGTHEN THE KNOWLEDGE AND CAPABILITIES OF APPLICANTS AND GRANTEES TO SUCCESSFULLY PARTICIPATE IN RHTP. KHI WILL USE INDIVIDUAL INTERACTIONS TO IDENTIFY RECURRING KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND IMPLEMENTATION NEEDS; TRANSLATE THOSE NEEDS INTO TRAINING, TOOLS AND OTHER BROADLY AVAILABLE RESOURCES; AND USE LESSONS FROM THOSE ACTIVITIES TO CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVE SUBSEQUENT TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE. THROUGH THIS CYCLE, INDIVIDUALIZED ASSISTANCE AND PROACTIVE EDUCATION WILL REINFORCE ONE ANOTHER AND BUILD THE CAPACITY OF PARTICIPATING ORGANIZATIONS TO ADDRESS SIMILAR NEEDS INDEPENDENTLY OVER TIME.

DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD, THE COUNTY WILL TRANSITION FROM A PRIMARILY VOLUNTEER-BASED EMS SYSTEM TO A HYBRID MODEL SUPPORTED BY FULL-TIME EMS PERSONNEL, 24/7 PARAMEDIC-LEVEL ADVANCED LIFE SUPPORT (ALS) COVERAGE, AND MODERN AMBULANCE INFRASTRUCTURE. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE HIRING THREE (3) FULL-TIME EMS PERSONNEL TO PROVIDE CONTINUOUS EMERGENCY RESPONSE COVERAGE FROM GOLDFIELD USING A 48/96 A-B-C SHIFT SCHEDULE; EXECUTING A CONTRACT WITH RURAL MEDEVAC ALLIANCE TO PROVIDE A DEDICATED 24/7 PARAMEDIC QUICK RESPONSE SERVICE VEHICLE (QRV) THAT RESPONDS TO ALL 911 CALLS COUNTYWIDE AND SUPPORTS PATIENT CARE DURING TRANSPORT; PURCHASING AND PLACING INTO SERVICE THREE (3) NEW TYPE I AMBULANCES STATIONED IN GOLDFIELD, SILVER PEAK, AND FISH LAKE VALLEY (DYER); IMPLEMENTING COORDINATED DISPATCH, RESPONSE, AND PATIENT CARE PROTOCOLS; AND PROVIDING ONGOING EMS TRAINING AND CONTINUING EDUCATION TO STRENGTHEN LOCAL WORKFORCE CAPACITY. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO ESTABLISH DATA COLLECTION AND PERFORMANCE MONITORING SYSTEMS TO EVALUATE SERVICE UTILIZATION, RESPONSE TIMES, STAFFING, AND PATIENT OUTCOMES AND TO GUIDE FUTURE EXPANSION OF THE COUNTY’S EMS SYSTEM.

NORTHERN NYE COUNTY HOSPITAL DISTRICT (NNCHD) WILL EXPAND AND STRENGTHEN EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES THROUGHOUT NORTHERN NYE COUNTY BY ESTABLISHING A PROFESSIONALLY STAFFED, 24/7 EMS RESPONSE MODEL SERVING TONOPAH, ROUND MOUNTAIN, AND SURROUNDING RURAL AND FRONTIER COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES SIGNIFICANT GAPS IN EMERGENCY RESPONSE CAPACITY CAUSED BY THE REGION’S VAST GEOGRAPHY, LONG TRANSPORT DISTANCES, LIMITED LOCAL HEALTHCARE INFRASTRUCTURE, AGING AMBULANCE RESOURCES, AND HISTORIC RELIANCE ON A SMALL VOLUNTEER EMS WORKFORCE. NORTHERN NYE COUNTY ENCOMPASSES APPROXIMATELY 11,685 SQUARE MILES AND HAS FEWER THAN 6,000 RESIDENTS. THE REGION HAS NO LOCAL HOSPITAL OR EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, AND PATIENTS REQUIRING HOSPITAL-LEVEL CARE MUST GENERALLY BE TRANSPORTED MORE THAN ONE HOUR, WITH TRAUMA-LEVEL CARE REQUIRING TRAVEL OF MORE THAN TWO HOURS ONE WAY. AMBULANCE TRANSPORTS CAN REMOVE A UNIT FROM LOCAL SERVICE FOR AS LONG AS SIX HOURS, SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCING EMERGENCY RESPONSE CAPACITY FOR THE REMAINING SERVICE AREA. NNCHD WILL COMPETITIVELY PROCURE THE EMS PROVIDER DURING THE INITIAL TWO MONTHS OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, WITH CONTRACTED SERVICE IMPLEMENTATION AND PERSONNEL DEPLOYMENT TO FOLLOW UPON COMPLETION OF THE PROCUREMENT PROCESS. DURING THE OCTOBER 1, 2026 THROUGH AUGUST 30, 2027 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE, NNCHD WILL CONTRACT WITH AN EMS PROVIDER TO ESTABLISH CONTINUOUS PROFESSIONAL AMBULANCE STAFFING IN BOTH TONOPAH AND ROUND MOUNTAIN. TWO AMBULANCE UNITS WILL BE STAFFED 24 HOURS PER DAY, SEVEN DAYS PER WEEK BY A TOTAL OF 12 EMT-LEVEL PROFESSIONALS, WITH SIX PERSONNEL SUPPORTING EACH LOCATION. PERSONNEL WILL RESPOND NOT ONLY WITHIN THEIR PRIMARY STATION AREAS BUT THROUGHOUT NORTHERN NYE COUNTY AS NEEDED. NNCHD WILL SUPPORT RECRUITMENT OF QUALIFIED EMS PROFESSIONALS, INCLUDING CURRENT VOLUNTEER RESPONDERS INTERESTED IN TRANSITIONING TO PAID POSITIONS, WHILE THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER WILL EMPLOY, ONBOARD, ADMINISTER, AND SUPERVISE THE WORKFORCE. EMT-LEVEL PERSONNEL WILL ALSO BE ENCOURAGED TO PURSUE ADVANCED EMT TRAINING TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF LOCALLY AVAILABLE ADVANCED PROVIDERS AND STRENGTHEN THE REGION’S LONG-TERM EMS WORKFORCE. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO ESTABLISH ONE 24/7 AEMT-LEVEL SUPERVISORY POSITION STAFFED BY THREE PROFESSIONALS. THIS POSITION WILL PROVIDE SCHEDULING AND OPERATIONAL COORDINATION, CLINICAL OVERSIGHT, PROTOCOL COMPLIANCE, PERFORMANCE MONITORING, COORDINATION WITH VOLUNTEER RESPONDERS AND REGIONAL HEALTHCARE PARTNERS, AND CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT. THE SUPERVISOR WILL SERVE AS THE PRIMARY OPERATIONAL CONTACT BETWEEN THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER AND NNCHD AND WILL HELP ENSURE CONSISTENT STANDARDS OF CARE ACROSS THE EXPANDED EMS SYSTEM. THE EXPANDED SERVICE WILL BUILD UPON NNCHD’S EXISTING LOCALLY FUNDED PARTNERSHIP WITH REMSA HEALTH, WHICH CURRENTLY PROVIDES ONE 24/7 PARAMEDIC-LEVEL POSITION BASED IN TONOPAH AND OPERATING A QUICK RESPONSE VEHICLE (QRV). THE PARAMEDIC/QRV PROVIDES ADVANCED EMERGENCY INTERVENTION AND CAN RESPOND EVEN WHEN AN AMBULANCE IS UNAVAILABLE BECAUSE OF A LONG-DISTANCE TRANSPORT. THE RHT-FUNDED EXPANSION WILL ADD STAFFED AMBULANCE CAPACITY AND SYSTEMWIDE SUPERVISION WHILE INTEGRATING WITH THIS EXISTING PARAMEDIC RESOURCE TO CREATE A MORE RELIABLE AND COORDINATED EMS RESPONSE SYSTEM. THE PROJECT WILL FURTHER IMPROVE EMS READINESS THROUGH THE ACQUISITION AND DEPLOYMENT OF TWO NEW TYPE I AMBULANCES, ONE ASSIGNED TO TONOPAH AND ONE TO ROUND MOUNTAIN, TOGETHER WITH UPDATED MEDICAL AND COMMUNICATIONS EQUIPMENT NECESSARY TO SUPPORT SAFE EMERGENCY RESPONSE AND TRANSPORT. EQUIPMENT WILL INCLUDE POWER-LOAD STRETCHERS, CARDIAC MONITORS, VENTILATORS, STAIR CHAIRS, RADIOS, IPADS, MOBILE DATA TERMINALS, MODEMS, COMPUTERS, AND RELATED EMS EQUIPMENT. THE CONTRACTED EMS PROVIDER WILL ALSO PROVIDE THE DISPATCH, COMMUNICATIONS, LOGISTICS, DATA MANAGEMENT, QUALITY ASSURANCE, AND ADMINISTRATIVE INFRASTRUCTURE NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE EXPANDED SYSTEM.

THE DEPARTMENT’S FLEET INCLUDES TWO AMBULANCES THAT HAVE REACHED THE END OF THEIR RELIABLE SERVICE LIFE: A 2002 FORD F-350 AMBULANCE STATIONED IN MINA, FOR WHICH REPLACEMENT PARTS ARE NO LONGER AVAILABLE, AND A 2012 MERCEDES SPRINTER AMBULANCE WITH 145,800 MILES. PATIENT-LIFT SYSTEMS ARE CURRENTLY INSTALLED IN THESE UNITS, BUT THE LIFTS ARE 14 YEARS OLD AND ARE DUE FOR REPLACEMENT. THROUGH THIS SUBAWARD, MINERAL COUNTY WILL (1) PROCURE AND PLACE INTO SERVICE TWO NEW WHEELED COACH TYPE 1 AMBULANCES (ONE 4X4 AND ONE 4X2) TO REPLACE THE 2002 FORD F-350 MINA UNIT AND THE 2012 SPRINTER, EACH EQUIPPED WITH NEW STRYKER POWER-LOAD NO-LIFT SYSTEMS TO REPLACE THE EXISTING 14-YEAR-OLD LIFTS, (2) PROCURE AND DEPLOY ADVANCED DIAGNOSTIC AND RESPIRATORY EQUIPMENT—INCLUDING THE HEROVENT TRANSPORT VENTILATOR, VSCAN AIR ULTRASOUND, POCKET-DOP, AND DIGITAL STETHOSCOPES—AND TRAIN ALL FIELD STAFF TO FULL PROFICIENCY IN THEIR USE, AND (3) BUILD A SUSTAINABLE, “GROW-YOUR-OWN” REGIONAL CLINICAL WORKFORCE PIPELINE THROUGH IN-HOUSE TRAINING, ADVANCING EMT-BASICS TO ADVANCED EMT (AEMT) LEVEL—MINERAL COUNTY EMS DOES NOT STAFF PARAMEDICS—WITH COURSE SEATS EXTENDED TO COMMUNITY RECRUITS FROM MINERAL COUNTY AND NEIGHBORING RURAL/FRONTIER COMMUNITIES THAT LACK LOCAL TRAINING CAPACITY, INCLUDING ESMERALDA COUNTY AND GABBS (NYE COUNTY), AND CERTIFYING STAFF IN WILDERNESS MEDICINE AND FARMEDIC RESPONSE. BASELINE METRICS: MINERAL COUNTY CURRENTLY OPERATES A 2002 FORD F-350 AMBULANCE STATIONED IN MINA FOR WHICH REPLACEMENT PARTS ARE NO LONGER AVAILABLE, AND A 2012 SPRINTER AMBULANCE WITH 145,800 MILES. BOTH UNITS HAVE PATIENT-LIFT SYSTEMS INSTALLED, BUT THOSE LIFTS ARE 14 YEARS OLD. THE DEPARTMENT HAS NO ONBOARD ADVANCED TRANSPORT VENTILATOR OR POINT-OF-CARE ULTRASOUND CAPABILITY, AND A LIMITED NUMBER OF STAFF ARE CREDENTIALED ABOVE THE EMT-BASIC. PROVIDER LIFT-RELATED INJURY INCIDENCE AND ALS-LEVEL BILLING CAPTURE ARE TRACKED BUT CURRENTLY LIMITED BY THE AGING FLEET, AGING LIFT EQUIPMENT, AND STAFFING GAPS DESCRIBED ABOVE. PROJECTED OUTCOME METRICS: BY THE END OF BUDGET PERIOD 1, MINERAL COUNTY PROJECTS: THE 2002 FORD F-350 MINA AMBULANCE AND THE 2012 SPRINTER (145,800 MILES) FULLY REPLACED BY TWO NEW TYPE 1 AMBULANCES (4X4 AND 4X2) IN DAILY SERVICE, EACH WITH A NEW STRYKER POWER-LOAD SYSTEM REPLACING THE 14-YEAR-OLD LIFTS, AND A MEASURABLE REDUCTION IN LIFT-RELATED STAFF INJURIES RELATIVE TO BASELINE; 100% OF FIELD STAFF PROFICIENT IN THE USE OF THE HEROVENT, VSCAN AIR, POCKET-DOP, AND DIGITAL STETHOSCOPES, VERIFIED THROUGH BI-MONTHLY HIGH-FIDELITY SIMULATIONS; AN INCREASED NUMBER OF STAFF HOLDING AEMT CREDENTIALS THROUGH IN-HOUSE TRAINING (MINERAL COUNTY EMS DOES NOT STAFF PARAMEDICS).

THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS RENOVATING THE RADIOLOGY DEPARTMENT SPACE TO HOUSE EQUIPMENT (THE PHILIPS RADIOGRAPHY 7300 C WITH AMBIENT LIGHTING SYSTEM) PURCHASED UNDER A PRIVATE SECTOR GRANT AWARD FROM THE LEONA M. AND HARRY B. HELMSLEY CHARITABLE TRUST. CURRENTLY, MGGH RELIES ON A 1993 BENNETT RADIOLOGY UNIT, WHICH NO LONGER HAS PARTS AVAILABLE, PLUS ITS OBSOLETE STATUS HAS MADE IT INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT TO SERVICE OVER THE LAST TWO YEARS. IN CONTRAST, THE PHILIPS RADIOGRAPHY 7300 C IS A SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER PERFORMANCE UNIT, WITH GREATER IMAGE CLARITY, AS WELL AS INTEGRATION WITH EMR AND TECHNOLOGY DEVICES FOR FACILITATING COLLABORATIVE CARE. NOTABLY, THE AMBIENT LIGHTING SYSTEM WILL HELP TO EASE FEARS AND ANXIETIES BY PATIENTS, INCLUDING THOSE WITH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISORDERS, AUTISM, AND OTHER CONDITIONS, WHO FIND CHANGES IN ROUTINES, AND MEDICAL ENCOUNTERS TO BE STRESSORS. REPEAT IMAGES WILL BE REDUCED BY USING THE PHILIPS RADIOGRAPHY 7300 C, WHILE ENSURING A CALM ENVIRONMENT WITH ITS AMBIENT LIGHTING SYSTEM. FURTHER, EXAM TIMES WILL BE REDUCED, THE POSITIONING PROCESS WILL BE EASIER, AND DIAGNOSTIC CONFIDENCE WILL BE ENHANCED WITH GREATER RELIABILITY. IT IS PARAMOUNT THAT THE NEWLY PURCHASED UNIT BE HOUSED WITHIN THE RADIOLOGY DEPARTMENT, AS THE ALTERNATIVE WOULD BE TO TRANSPORT PATIENTS OUTSIDE OF THE HOSPITAL FACILITY TO ANOTHER BUILDING AND EXPOSE THEM TO THE ELEMENTS.

subaward_description: GREAT BASIN COLLEGE (GBC) WILL RENOVATE AND FURNISH SIX EXISTING APARTMENTS ON THE GBC-ELKO CAMPUS TO PROVIDE MOVE-IN-READY HOUSING FOR MEDICAL STUDENTS, PHYSICIAN RESIDENTS, NURSING STUDENTS, ALLIED HEALTH STUDENTS, AND OTHER HEALTHCARE TRAINEES COMPLETING RURAL CLINICAL ROTATIONS IN NORTHEASTERN NEVADA. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES A PRACTICAL BUT SIGNIFICANT BARRIER TO EXPANDING RURAL CLINICAL TRAINING: THE LIMITED AVAILABILITY OF AFFORDABLE, FURNISHED, SHORT-TERM HOUSING FOR TRAINEES COMING TO ELKO COUNTY. DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD, GBC WILL RENOVATE BUILDING A OF THE COLLEGE PARKWAY APARTMENTS, WHICH INCLUDES THREE THREE-BEDROOM AND THREE TWO-BEDROOM UNITS. EACH APARTMENT IS APPROXIMATELY 615 SQUARE FEET AND INCLUDES A KITCHEN, BATHROOM, LIVING SPACE, AND LAUNDRY AREA. GBC WILL COMPETITIVELY PROCURE A LICENSED GENERAL CONTRACTOR TO COMPLETE THE WORK. RENOVATIONS WILL INCLUDE INTERIOR PAINTING AND FLOORING; LIGHTING UPGRADES; KITCHEN AND BATHROOM IMPROVEMENTS; CABINETRY AND COUNTERTOPS; DOORS AND HARDWARE; PLUMBING AND HVAC IMPROVEMENTS; AND EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENTS, INCLUDING STUCCO, TRIM, WINDOWS, AND GUTTERS. FOLLOWING RENOVATION, GBC WILL PURCHASE AND INSTALL THE FURNITURE, APPLIANCES, FIXTURES, AND HOUSEHOLD ITEMS NEEDED TO MAKE ALL SIX UNITS FULLY FURNISHED AND READY FOR OCCUPANCY. GREAT BASIN COLLEGE WILL ALSO WORK WITH ITS HEALTHCARE AND ACADEMIC PARTNERS TO COORDINATE CLINICAL ROTATION SCHEDULES AND HOUSING NEEDS. PARTNERS INCLUDE NORTHEASTERN NEVADA REGIONAL HOSPITAL (NNRH), NEVADA HEALTH CENTERS (NVHC), THE UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, RENO (UNR), THE UNIVERSITY OF NEVADA, LAS VEGAS (UNLV), NEVADA STATE UNIVERSITY (NSU), AND OTHER HEALTHCARE AND ACADEMIC PARTNERS AS OPPORTUNITIES DEVELOP. THE COMPLETED APARTMENTS WILL PRIMARILY HOUSE HEALTHCARE TRAINEES COMPLETING CLINICAL ROTATIONS IN ELKO AND SURROUNDING RURAL COMMUNITIES. WHEN SPACE IS AVAILABLE, THEY MAY ALSO PROVIDE TEMPORARY HOUSING FOR LICENSED HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS RELOCATING TO THE AREA OR TRAVELING MEDICAL STAFF. THE HEALTHCARE OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT EXTENDS BEYOND THE RENOVATION OF SIX APARTMENTS. BY PROVIDING RELIABLE HOUSING FOR HEALTHCARE TRAINEES, GBC AND ITS PARTNERS WILL REMOVE AN IDENTIFIED BARRIER TO RURAL CLINICAL PLACEMENTS AND INCREASE THE REGION’S CAPACITY TO EXPOSE FUTURE HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS TO RURAL PRACTICE. THIS INVESTMENT WILL SUPPORT A STRONGER PIPELINE OF PHYSICIANS, NURSES, ADVANCED PRACTICE PROVIDERS, AND ALLIED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITH DIRECT EXPERIENCE SERVING RURAL NEVADA. OVER TIME, INCREASING THE NUMBER OF HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS WHO TRAIN IN NORTHEASTERN NEVADA WILL SUPPORT PROVIDER RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO PRIMARY, PREVENTIVE, AND SPECIALTY HEALTHCARE SERVICES THROUGHOUT THE REGION.

THIS PROGRAM SEEKS TO RESHAPE HEALTHCARE DELIVERY TO BETTER ALIGN WITH COMMUNITY NEEDS AND IMPROVE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF RURAL SYSTEMS OF CARE. PLANNING AWARDS WILL ALSO BE USED TO ESTABLISH REGIONAL PARTNERSHIPS, PARTICIPATE IN TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND BUILD INITIAL INFRASTRUCTURE.
